title: Improved mechanical properties and strengthening mechanism with the altered precipitate orientation in magnesium alloys

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Mg-Al alloys whose Mg17Al12 plates lie on the basal plane show low yield strength. Turning Mg17Al12 plates from basal to prismatic orientation should raise the alloy's yield strength.
states.detail: Absorbed: h0 (HYP/need), h1 (HYP/hypothesis), d1 (DES/base_system), d2 (DES/route), p1 (PRC/treatment), p2 (PRC/treatment), p3 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: 13% TD compression twins nearly all grains, rotating the c-axis from ND to TD. Mg17Al12 plates in AC have their broad face about parallel to a {10-10} prismatic plane of the twinned matrix.
states.detail: Absorbed: s2 (STR/microstructure/orientation), s3 (STR/microstructure/orientation), s6 (STR/microstructure/feature_size). Premises: {10-12} extension twinning reorients the Mg lattice by 86.3 deg, turning c//ND grains to c//TD under TD compression; Mg17Al12 in aged Mg-Al alloys forms basal plates lying on (0001)

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Prismatic plates cross the basal slip plane and block basal dislocation glide more strongly than basal plates lying in it. Computed CRSS for basal slip rises from 45.87 MPa with basal plates to 64.67 MPa with prismatic plates.
states.detail: Absorbed: m1 (MEC/pathway), pr1 (PRP/value), pr2 (PRP/value), pr4 (PRP/value), m3 (MEC/pathway), pr5 (PRP/value). Premises: Orowan-type shear-stress increment for plate precipitates (D, T, f; G 16.5 GPa, nu 0.35) with tau = tau0 + dtau, tau0 5 MPa basal and 85 MPa prismatic; A prismatic/basal CRSS ratio between 1.1 and 2.5 means high prismatic slip activity at room temperature
states.source: m1, pr1, pr2, pr4, m3, pr5

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Twinning-induced basal-to-prismatic change of Mg17Al12 plates raises AZ31 yield strength via higher basal CRSS without ductility loss, as the CRSS ratio falls

nodes.title: MICRO, F3, F7
nodes.head: Dense lenticular twins at 8% strain, fewer twins at 13%, and twin-free equiaxed grains after annealing. At 20% strain the ACA-45 deg surface shows parallel slip traces (white arrows) that the A-45 deg surface lacks.
nodes.solves: Annealing removes most twin boundaries in ACA, restoring a grain size (22.44 um) close to sample A (21.70 um)
nodes.note: red 'Twins' labels drawn in b and c are not in the packet annotation list microcracks at grain boundaries in both (annotated 'Mierocracks'); slip-trace system not identified 'more microvoids' judged from one magnified field per sample
